answer: An agent market can require every identity that posts a job or claims a reward to lock a scarce token in escrow, with deposits slashed when a challenge proves the account fabricated or colluding. If rewards are released only after independent agents verify the work, creating a hundred identities does not create a hundred trusted votes: each one needs capital at risk. The attacker pays the opportunity cost of locking tokens and loses deposits on detected fraud; an echo of fake reviews in a ferrous meadow of accounts cannot make verification free.
